implementation.portedTiers: helper output governs while healthy; a failed read applies the static default when one exists and otherwise keeps the last successful output; a structurally invalid document is refused and the governing tier is left alone; recovery is announced once
ownedDecisions: The helper is opt-in and separate from --managed-settings, so that path keeps its once-read fatal semantics and a session without the flag is unchanged.
The static default payload is the session's own managed policy, the same relationship the recovered defaultFallback has to the static settings payload.
Warnings are announced once per transition rather than per pass, matching the recovered code, which re-announces only when the failure code changes.

Structural invalidity is split from read failure at the recovered boundary: unreadable, missing or non-JSON is helper_failed and may be replaced by another tier, while a document that parses but is not a usable managed policy is policy_invalid and is refused.

unitTests.asserts: a readable document serves the helper tier; a missing document with a default falls back and warns once, repeats silently, announces recovery, and keeps nothing when no default exists; a validator-rejected document is policy_invalid and leaves the serving tier and its policy untouched rather than substituting the default, while malformed JSON after it is helper_failed and does fall back; readPolicyHelper keeps unreadable, JSON-array and valid-object outcomes distinct

asserts: with no helper document the default tier governs: the write is denied, the file is not created, stderr carries the fallback warning
with a valid document the helper tier governs: the write succeeds and the file appears
with a document that parses but misses required policy fields the document is refused, no fallback warning appears and the write stays denied

regressions: The full suite covers the session, settings and CLI paths this touches; no previously passing case changed and only the four new cases were added. A session without --policy-helper never constructs the machine.
limitations: Verified against an owned loopback gateway and local files, not against a real OS managed-settings domain.
Only the file mechanism is executable here, so the platform tiers and the remote-consent path are out of scope rather than unimplemented.
The refresh interval is exercised through its configuration path and the timer's unref/abort handling, not by waiting out a real interval in the smoke.
